IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives Pearson, Johnson, Smith, Wilcox, Schmick, Haler, and Harris

Bill.BriefDescription: Removing the payment of vehicle license fees and taxes from the issuance of gold star license plates.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to gold star license plates; amending RCW46.18.245; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 46.18.245 and 2010 c 161 s 621 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A registered owner who is the mother or father of a member ofthe United States armed forces who died while in service to his or hercountry, or as a result of his or her service, may apply to thedepartment for special gold star license plates for use on a motorvehicle. The registered owner must: (a) Be a resident of this state; (b) Provide certification from the Washington state department ofveterans affairs that the registered owner qualifies for the speciallicense plate under this section; and (c) Be recorded as the registered owner of the motor vehicle onwhich the gold star license plates will be displayed((; and (d) Pay all fees and taxes required by law for registering themotor vehicle)). (2) Gold star license plates must be issued: p. 1 HB 2248 (a) Only for motor vehicles owned by qualifying applicants; and (b) Without payment of any license plate fee, vehicle license fee,or excise tax. (3) Gold star license plates must be replaced, free of charge, ifthe license plates become lost, stolen, damaged, defaced, or destroyed. (4) Gold star license plates may be transferred from one motorvehicle to another motor vehicle owned by the mother or father, asdescribed in subsection (1) of this section, upon application to thedepartment, county auditor or other agent, or subagent appointed by thedirector.
